extracted.intended_audience: research authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to Econometrica (economics researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting original research manuscripts, corrections/comments, supplemental material, and revisions to the journal Econometrica. Covers eligibility, formatting, fees, supplemental/replication material, and procedural requirements for submission and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author membership eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a paper to Econometrica, at least one author must be a member of the Econometric Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the authors is a member, they must join (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and concurrent_submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must present original, unpublished work that is not under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A working paper version should be publicly available, such as on a personal website or other public repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic_submission_and_file_format
rubrics_metrics.description: Econometrica accepts only electronic submissions; papers should be submitted in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the online submission link on the site to start an online submission. It is recommended, though not required, that authors use the LaTeX template available from the journal’s support page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission_fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission fee of US$125 for regular members and US$50 for student members applies to all new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission fee must be paid by credit card at the time of submission. Submission fees are non-refundable, including for papers rejected without review. Individuals in World Bank low-income countries are exempt. Invited resubmissions require only membership (no fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication_fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers will incur a publication fee of 50% of the production cost per page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee applies to all typeset material and will be collected after final proofs are approved but before publication; invoiced at prevailing rate. Individuals in World Bank low-income or lower-middle-income countries are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page_limit_main_paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be limited to 45 pages, including references and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to the page limits may be granted upon request; authors seeking to submit a paper exceeding the allowed length must obtain permission from the Editor via email before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting_requirements_font_spacing_margins
rubrics_metrics.description: The font size must be at least 12 points, line spacing at least 1.5, and all margins at least 1.25 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules apply to the entire manuscript, including references and appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization_and_readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Material should be organized to enhance readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, footnotes and figures should not be placed at the end of the document. Pages should be numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title_page_and_abstract_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page should include an abstract of no more than 150 words, keywords, and full author affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author_order_statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Econometrica does not allow the use of \textcircled{r} to indicate a certified random order for authors’ names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are free to specify the methods used to determine author order in a footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental_appendix_policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may include a supplemental appendix with non-essential additional results and robustness analyses that are not critical to the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental appendix should be clearly labeled, should not exceed 25 pages, and must follow the same formatting requirements (font size, line spacing, and margins) as the main text. Supplemental appendices are posted under 'Supplemental Material' and are not typeset. The main paper (including any in-paper appendices but excluding the supplemental appendix) must be self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication_and_experimental_supporting_documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions with empirical, experimental, or simulation results are required to include additional supporting documentation per the Replication Policy and Experimental Papers Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation may be submitted with the main paper via the online submission form and does not count toward page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental_files_handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Large files should be compressed into a .zip format; if submitting more than two supplemental files, combine them into a single .zip file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover_letter_content_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover letter should be included only if it contains information relevant to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, if the author has submitted related work elsewhere, they must provide details. If the submission relates to a previously rejected submission to Econometrica, the author should explain why it is sufficiently different. Any request for exemption from the journal’s Editorial Procedures and Policies must be stated explicitly at the time of initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections_vs_comments_definitions_and_scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections and comments are short articles addressing a paper previously published in the relevant journal: a correction identifies an error/flaw and aims to restore factual accuracy; a comment is more substantial and may elaborate a solution or generalization that changes interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are frequently (but needn't be) written by original authors; comments typically by independent authors. Titles should be 'Correction to ‘‘[original paper title]’’' or 'Comment on ‘‘[original paper title]’’'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction_comment_author_contact_requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting a correction or comment requires contacting at least one of the original authors, unless an original author is part of the submitting author team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original authors do not respond within two months, this should be noted in the submission. The correspondence with the original authors should be included with the journal submission. The original authors may be invited to reply to any accepted correction or comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision_offer_validity_and_extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An offer to revise a paper is typically valid for 12 months from the decision date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted at the discretion of the handling Co-Editor but must be requested within that 12-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement_to_editorial_policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a paper indicates that the authors agree to abide by the journal’s Editorial Procedures and Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any questions, contact the Editorial Office at the provided email address.
